author.heading: About Daniel Dennett
author.bio: Daniel Dennett (1942–2024) was an American philosopher whose work connected philosophy of mind with cognitive science and evolutionary biology. He taught at Tufts for more than fifty years and directed its Center for Cognitive Studies; his books include Consciousness Explained and Breaking the Spell.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Consciousness Explained proposes a model informed by neuroscience, psychology and artificial intelligence. The aphorism warns that being unable to imagine an alternative is not the same as proving the alternative impossible. It belongs to that book’s challenge to intuitive pictures of the mind, rather than a claim that imagination can settle every philosophical question.
